chunks.content: PS20115MLM4-2 is an electrical schematic titled "MOD-LINX POWER SUPPLY ASSY: 24VDC 20AMP OUTPUT, 115VAC-1 PHASE INPUT, MOD LINX MASTER 4 DRIVE CARDS, SCHEMATIC". Dated 2017-09-19. It documents the Mod-Linx Power Supply Assembly, Master, 4 Drive Cards. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. This drawing is the confidential property of CONVEYX CORP. and is transmitted in confidence. The reproduction, disclosure, or use, in whole or part, of the design or the details contained herein is prohibited without the express written permission of Conveyx Corp. It references the related drawings: MXCS-M9, MXCS-M11, MXCS-P9, MXCS-P11. Drawing notes: Input: 115VAC 1 phase, 60Hz. L1 = 4.16 FLA @115VAC. SCCR = 5kA. NOTE: Keep all DC wires 4" minimum clearance from 115VAC wires. NOTE: Individual wires to all points of termination. Do not double place wires. Label all wires and cables 1" from end. NOTE (LT1 cable): Remove white and brown wire at insulation, heat shrink exposed end. Title-block stamp: REVISED - destroy previous drawing with the same number. Date 04/08/2020. Sheet size is D. The title block has no separate revision field; the 'D' that appears in the side tab and the SIZE box is the sheet size, NOT a revision letter. Safety note: The need for safety devices varies with each application of this product. This drawing may not include all appropriate safety devices for your application. As systems integrator, please advise your customer of devices that are appropriate for his/her application, based on your safety assessment. Devices may include, but are not limited to those such as, additional guarding, safety controls, barricades, end stops, etc. Compliance with all federal, state, OSHA and local laws or codes are the responsibility of both you, as the systems integrator/distributor, and the end user. Drawing file/part reference in the side tab: CXC_MXPS-ASSY.

PLG1 is a cable plug on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Power-in plug, Leviton LEV2611, on the POWER IN 115VAC cable. Pins B (line), W (neutral) and G (ground). Function: Brings 115VAC single-phase supply power into the power supply assembly. Ratings - voltage: 115VAC, phase: 1, frequency: 60Hz, pins: 3. It operates in the 115VAC power domain. Its normal state is energized when upstream supply is on. Part number LEV2611. It is also referred to as power in plug, input plug, LEV2611. It is drawn in the top-left area of the schematic.

PLG2 is a cable plug on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Power-out plug, Leviton LEV2613, on the POWER OUT 115VAC cable. Pins B (line), W (neutral) and G (ground). Wired in parallel with PLG1 at the L1/N/GND terminals. Function: Passes 115VAC supply power through to the next machine in the line (daisy chain). Ratings - voltage: 115VAC, phase: 1, frequency: 60Hz, pins: 3. It operates in the 115VAC power domain. Its normal state is energized when upstream supply is on. Part number LEV2613. It is also referred to as power out plug, output plug, LEV2613. It is drawn in the top-left area of the schematic.

TB-L1 is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked L1 where the 115VAC line conductors of PLG1 and PLG2 land. Function: Common the 115VAC line between the input plug, the output plug and the disconnect. It operates in the 115VAC power domain. Its normal state is energized when upstream supply is on. It is also referred to as terminal L1, L1 terminal. It is drawn in the top-left area of the schematic.

TB-N is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked N where the 115VAC neutral conductors of PLG1 and PLG2 land. Function: Common the 115VAC neutral between the input plug, the output plug and the disconnect. It operates in the 115VAC power domain. Its normal state is at neutral potential. It is also referred to as terminal N, neutral terminal. It is drawn in the top-left area of the schematic.

TB-GND-A is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Terminal marked GND where the green ground conductors of PLG1 and PLG2 land; bonded to the earth ground symbol. Function: Bonds the plug ground conductors to the panel protective earth. It operates in the 0V_common power domain. Its normal state is bonded to earth. It is also referred to as terminal GND, plug ground terminal. It is drawn in the top-left area of the schematic.

DISC1 is a switch on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Panel disconnect switch. Three poles drawn L1/T1, L2/T2 and L3/T3; only L1-T1 (line) and L3-T3 (neutral) are wired on this drawing. L2-T2 is spare. Function: Manually isolates the 115VAC supply feeding the power supply assembly. Ratings - poles: 3, poles_used: 2. It operates in the 115VAC power domain. Its normal state is closed when the panel is switched on. It is also referred to as panel disconnect, main disconnect, DISC1. It is drawn in the top-centre-left area of the schematic.

CB1 is a circuit breaker on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. 8 amp circuit breaker in the 115VAC line ahead of the power supply. Terminals 1 (line from DISC1:T1) and 2 (load to PS1:L1). Function: Over-current protection for the 115VAC feed to power supply PS1. Ratings - current: 8A, poles: 1, voltage: 115VAC. It operates in the 115VAC power domain. Its normal state is closed (ON). It is also referred to as 8 amp breaker, 8AMP CIRCUIT BREAKER, main breaker. It is drawn in the top-centre area of the schematic.

PS1 is a power supply on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. 20 amp power supply converting 115VAC single-phase input to 24VDC output. Input terminals L1, N and GND; output terminals + (plus) and two - (minus) terminals. Function: Supplies 24VDC to the control circuits, the drive cards and the downstream machine interfaces. Ratings - input: 115VAC 1 phase 60Hz, output: 24VDC, current: 20A. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is energized whenever CB1 and DISC1 are closed. It is also referred to as 20AMP POWER SUPPLY, 24V power supply, PSU, power supply. It is drawn in the top-centre area of the schematic.

TB-GND-B is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Two-point terminal marked GND carrying the door ground and the power-supply ground; bonded to the earth ground symbol. Function: Bonds the enclosure door and the power supply chassis to protective earth. It operates in the 0V_common power domain. Its normal state is bonded to earth. It is also referred to as GND terminal, door ground terminal. It is drawn in the top-centre area of the schematic.

DOOR-GND is a ground on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Door ground connection point shown at the left of the GND terminal. Function: Bonds the enclosure door to protective earth. It operates in the 0V_common power domain. Its normal state is bonded to earth. It is also referred to as DOOR GND, door earth. It is drawn in the top-centre area of the schematic.

EARTH is a ground on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Protective earth (ground) reference, drawn as two earth symbols - one below TB-GND-A and one below TB-GND-B. Function: Panel protective earth reference for the whole assembly. It operates in the 0V_common power domain. Its normal state is at earth potential. It is also referred to as earth, ground, PE, protective earth. It is drawn in the top area of the schematic.

CB2 is a circuit breaker on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. 20 amp circuit breaker on the 24VDC output of PS1. Terminals 1 (from PS1:+) and 2 (to the 24E-1 distribution terminal). Function: Over-current protection for the whole 24VDC distribution bus (net 24E-1). Ratings - current: 20A, poles: 1, voltage: 24VDC. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is closed (ON). It is also referred to as 20 amp breaker, 20AMP CIRCUIT BREAKER, DC breaker. It is drawn in the top-centre-right area of the schematic.

TB-24E1-A is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Main 24VDC distribution terminal block marked 24E-1, on the left edge of the sheet. Eight points: the feed from CB2:2 plus seven outgoing circuits. Function: Distributes +24VDC (net 24E-1) to the secondary 24E-1 terminal block, both start/stop switches, the circuit-1 light and the CR-ON, CR-BP and CR-SW relay coils. Ratings - points: 8. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is energized whenever CB2 is closed. It is also referred to as 24E-1 terminal, main 24V terminal block, 24VDC distribution terminal. It is drawn in the left edge area of the schematic.

TB-24E1-B is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Secondary 24VDC distribution terminal block marked 24E-1, in the centre of the sheet. Fed from TB-24E1-A; five outgoing circuits. Function: Distributes +24VDC to the reverse breaker, the speed controller, the CR-ON and CR-BP run contacts and the 5-pin external receptacle. Ratings - points: 6. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is energized whenever CB2 is closed. It is also referred to as 24E-1 terminal, secondary 24V terminal block. It is drawn in the centre area of the schematic.

TB-0V is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Tall multi-point 0V terminal strip labelled TERMINAL'S, on the right of the sheet. Every 0V (DC common) return on the drawing lands here. Function: Commons the 24VDC return (0V) for the whole assembly. It operates in the 0V_common power domain. Its normal state is at 0V. It is also referred to as 0V terminal, TERMINAL'S, common terminal strip, DC common. It is drawn in the right area of the schematic.

SPD1 is a speed controller on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Speed controller. Three terminals: 1 = +24V, 2 = 0V, 3 = SPEED. Function: Sets the conveyor speed reference sent out on the SPD signal to the drive cards. Ratings - supply: 24VDC, terminals: 3. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is energized whenever CB2 is closed. It is also referred to as SPEED CONTROLER, speed controller, speed pot. It is drawn in the top-right area of the schematic.

TB-SPD is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked SPD carrying the speed signal. Function: Junction point for the speed reference between SPD1 and the external receptacle. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is carries the speed reference. It is also referred to as SPD terminal, speed terminal. It is drawn in the top-right area of the schematic.

REVERSE-CB is a circuit breaker on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. 5 amp circuit breaker labelled REVERSE. Terminals 1 (from 24E-1) and 2 (to the DIR net). NOTE: on this machine family this breaker is used as a MANUAL SWITCH, not as over-current protection - it selects/enables the reverse (DIR) direction path. It is a breaker only because it DIN-rail mounts conveniently. Function: Manually enables the reverse direction signal (DIR) sent to the drive cards. Ratings - current: 5A, poles: 1. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is open (reverse not selected) unless the operator switches it on. It is also referred to as REVERSE 5AMP CIRCUIT BREAKER, reverse breaker, reverse switch, direction switch. It is drawn in the centre area of the schematic.

TB-DIR is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked DIR carrying the direction signal. Function: Junction point for the direction signal between the reverse breaker and the external receptacle. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is de-energized unless the reverse breaker is closed. It is also referred to as DIR terminal, direction terminal. It is drawn in the centre area of the schematic.

PB1 is a push button on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Start/stop switch #1: a lighted push button with a red (R) lamp for the open/stopped state and a green (G) lamp for the closed/running state. Four terminals: 1 = +24VDC in, 2 = spare (to the PB1-SP terminal), 3 = 0V common, 4 = switched 24V signal out. Function: Operator start/stop control that energizes relay CR1. Ratings - terminals: 4, supply: 24VDC. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is open (not pressed) - red lamp lit. It is also referred to as PB1 START/STOP SWITCH, start/stop switch 1, start stop button 1, lighted push button 1. It is drawn in the left area of the schematic.

PB2 is a push button on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Start/stop switch #2: a lighted push button with a red (R) lamp for the open/stopped state and a green (G) lamp for the closed/running state. Four terminals: 1 = +24VDC in, 2 = spare (to the PB2-SP terminal), 3 = 0V common, 4 = switched 24V signal out. Function: Operator start/stop control that energizes relay CR2. Ratings - terminals: 4, supply: 24VDC. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is open (not pressed) - red lamp lit. It is also referred to as PB2 START/STOP SWITCH, start/stop switch 2, start stop button 2, lighted push button 2. It is drawn in the left area of the schematic.

TB-PB1SP is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked PB1-SP carrying the spare conductor of the PB1 start/stop cable. The conductor is landed but is not used elsewhere on this drawing. Function: Parks the spare white conductor of the PB1 start/stop cable. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is unused / spare. It is also referred to as PB1-SP terminal, PB1 spare terminal. It is drawn in the left area of the schematic.

TB-PB2SP is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked PB2-SP carrying the spare conductor of the PB2 start/stop cable. The conductor is landed but is not used elsewhere on this drawing. Function: Parks the spare white conductor of the PB2 start/stop cable. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is unused / spare. It is also referred to as PB2-SP terminal, PB2 spare terminal. It is drawn in the left area of the schematic.

LT1 is a indicator light on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Circuit 1 light with cable - a green indicator lamp on a 4-conductor cable. Black = 24E-1 (+24VDC), blue = 0V; the brown and white conductors are NOT CONNECTED and must be cut back at the insulation and heat-shrunk. Function: Indicates that the 24VDC control circuit (circuit 1) is powered. Ratings - conductors: 4, conductors_used: 2. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is lit whenever CB2 is closed. It is also referred to as CIRCUIT 1 LIGHT WITH CABLE, circuit 1 light, power on light. It is drawn in the left-centre area of the schematic.

CR1 is a relay on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Control relay CR1. Legend on the drawing: 'CR1: MODLINX PB1 START / STOP, 1N.O.' Coil terminals A1/A2; one normally-open contact 11-14. Function: Energized by start/stop switch PB1; its N.O. contact 11-14 is the first element of the two-in-series start/stop permissive chain. Ratings - coil_voltage: 24VDC, contacts: 1 N.O. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is de-energized (contact 11-14 open). It is also referred to as CR1, MODLINX PB1 START/STOP relay, start stop relay 1, relay CR-1. It is drawn in the right-centre area of the schematic.

CR2 is a relay on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Control relay CR2. Legend on the drawing: 'CR2: MODLINX PB2 START / STOP, 1N.O.' Coil terminals A1/A2; one normally-open contact 11-14. Function: Energized by start/stop switch PB2; its N.O. contact 11-14 is the second element of the two-in-series start/stop permissive chain. Ratings - coil_voltage: 24VDC, contacts: 1 N.O. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is de-energized (contact 11-14 open). It is also referred to as CR2, MODLINX PB2 START/STOP relay, start stop relay 2, relay CR-2. It is drawn in the right-centre area of the schematic.

CR-ON is a relay on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Control relay CR-ON. Legend on the drawing: 'CR-ON: MODLINX RUN, RUN SIGNAL TO CARDS, 1N.O.' Coil terminals A1/A2; one normally-open contact 11-14. Function: The run relay. When energized its N.O. contact 11-14 puts 24VDC on the RUN net, which sends the run signal to the drive cards and makes the machine run. Ratings - coil_voltage: 24VDC, contacts: 1 N.O. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is de-energized (machine stopped). It is also referred to as CR-ON, MODLINX RUN relay, run relay, CR ON. It is drawn in the right-centre area of the schematic.

CR-BP is a relay on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Control relay CR-BP. Legend on the drawing: 'CR-BP: RUN BYPASS RELAY, 1N.C., 1N.O.' Coil terminals A1/A2; one normally-closed contact 11-12 and one normally-open contact 21-24. Function: The run bypass relay. When energized its N.O. contact 21-24 puts 24VDC directly on the RUN net (bypassing CR-ON), and its N.C. contact 11-12 opens, breaking the link between the discharge signal 111 and net 110. Ratings - coil_voltage: 24VDC, contacts: 1 N.C. + 1 N.O. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is de-energized (11-12 closed, 21-24 open). It is also referred to as CR-BP, RUN BYPASS RELAY, bypass relay, run bypass relay. It is drawn in the bottom-right area of the schematic.

CR-SW is a relay on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Control relay CR-SW. Legend on the drawing: 'CR-SW: SWITCH RELAY, SWITCH CIRCUIT ON, 1N.O.' Coil terminals A1/A2; one normally-open contact 11-14. Function: The switch relay. Its coil returns through net 130, which leaves this drawing at the discharge interface, so it can only be energized by the downstream (subordinate) machine. When energized its N.O. contact 11-14 pulls net 110 to 0V. Ratings - coil_voltage: 24VDC, contacts: 1 N.O. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is de-energized (contact 11-14 open). It is also referred to as CR-SW, SWITCH RELAY, switch relay, CR SW. It is drawn in the bottom-right area of the schematic.

BYPASS-CB is a circuit breaker on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. 5 amp circuit breaker labelled BYPASS. Terminals 1 (from net 120) and 2 (to net 125). NOTE: on this machine family this breaker is used as a MANUAL SWITCH, not as over-current protection - it enables the bypass control path to the CR-BP coil. It is a breaker only because it DIN-rail mounts conveniently. Function: Manually enables the bypass control path that energizes relay CR-BP. Ratings - current: 5A, poles: 1. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is open (bypass not selected) unless the operator switches it on. It is also referred to as BYPASS 5AMP CIRCUIT BREAKER, bypass breaker, bypass switch. It is drawn in the bottom-centre area of the schematic.

TB-RUN is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked RUN carrying the run signal. Function: Commons the run signal from the CR-ON and CR-BP contacts and sends it to the external receptacle. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is de-energized when the machine is stopped. It is also referred to as RUN terminal, run signal terminal. It is drawn in the centre area of the schematic.

TB-110 is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Four-point terminal block marked 110 carrying the start/stop signal net. Function: Commons net 110 between the CR-SW contact, the infeed interface, the CR-ON coil return and the CR-BP normally-closed contact. Ratings - points: 4. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is carries the start/stop signal. It is also referred to as 110 terminal, terminal 110, start stop signal terminal. It is drawn in the centre-right area of the schematic.

TB-120 is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Three-point terminal block marked 120 carrying the start/stop permissive net. Function: Commons net 120 between the CR1/CR2 series contacts, the machine interfaces and the bypass breaker. Ratings - points: 3. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is carries the start/stop permissive. It is also referred to as 120 terminal, terminal 120. It is drawn in the bottom-left-centre area of the schematic.

TB-130 is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Two-point terminal block marked 130 carrying the CR-SW coil return net. Function: Commons net 130 between the CR-SW coil return and the machine interfaces. Ratings - points: 2. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is carries the switch-relay coil return. It is also referred to as 130 terminal, terminal 130. It is drawn in the bottom-centre-right area of the schematic.

RECEPT1 is a connector receptacle on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. 5-pin micro (M12) female receptacle for the external device connection. The five conductors are, in drawing order top to bottom: SPD brown 18AWG, DIR grey 18AWG, RUN black 18AWG, 0V white 18AWG and 24E-1 blue 18AWG. Their colours follow the standard M12 5-pin cordset code (1 brown, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 black, 5 grey), so the drawing order maps to standard pins 1, 5, 4, 2 and 3 respectively. Function: Carries 24VDC power, 0V, and the run, direction and speed signals out to the external drive-card devices. Ratings - pins: 5, style: M12 micro, female. It operates in the 24VDC power domain. Its normal state is energized whenever CB2 is closed. It is also referred to as 5-PIN MICRO FEMALE RECEPTACLE, 5 pin receptacle, external device connector, micro receptacle. It is drawn in the top-right area of the schematic.

INFEED1 is a connector receptacle on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Infeed interface #1, female 6-pin mini receptacle. Conductors: 110 blue 16AWG, 0V green 16AWG, 120 red 16AWG, 130 orange 16AWG, IINSP1 black 16AWG, IINSP2 white 16AWG. Function: Connects this master machine to the upstream (infeed) machine, carrying the start/stop signal, common, permissive and inspection signals. Ratings - pins: 6, style: 6-pin mini, female. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is connected to the upstream machine. It is also referred to as INFEED INTERFACE #1, infeed interface, infeed receptacle, female 6-pin mini receptacle. It is drawn in the centre-bottom area of the schematic.

DISCHARGE1 is a cable plug on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Discharge interface #1, male 6-pin mini cable. Conductors: 111 blue 16AWG, 0V green 16AWG, 120 red 16AWG, 130 orange 16AWG, DINSP1 black 16AWG, DINSP2 white 16AWG. Function: Connects this master machine to the downstream (discharge / subordinate) machine, carrying the start/stop signal, common, permissive and inspection signals. Ratings - pins: 6, style: 6-pin mini, male. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is connected to the downstream machine. It is also referred to as DISCHARGE INTERFACE #1, discharge interface, discharge cable, male 6-pin mini cable. It is drawn in the centre-bottom area of the schematic.

TB-IINSP1 is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked IINSP1 carrying the infeed inspection signal IINSP1. The signal is landed here and does not go anywhere else on this drawing. Function: Lands the IINSP1 inspection signal from the infeed interface. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is carries an inspection signal. It is also referred to as IINSP1 terminal. It is drawn in the centre-bottom area of the schematic.

TB-IINSP2 is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked IINSP2 carrying the infeed inspection signal IINSP2. The signal is landed here and does not go anywhere else on this drawing. Function: Lands the IINSP2 inspection signal from the infeed interface. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is carries an inspection signal. It is also referred to as IINSP2 terminal. It is drawn in the centre-bottom area of the schematic.

TB-DINSP1 is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked DINSP1 carrying the discharge inspection signal DINSP1. The signal is landed here and does not go anywhere else on this drawing. Function: Lands the DINSP1 inspection signal from the discharge interface. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is carries an inspection signal. It is also referred to as DINSP1 terminal. It is drawn in the centre-bottom area of the schematic.

TB-DINSP2 is a terminal block on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. Single-point terminal marked DINSP2 carrying the discharge inspection signal DINSP2. The signal is landed here and does not go anywhere else on this drawing. Function: Lands the DINSP2 inspection signal from the discharge interface. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is carries an inspection signal. It is also referred to as DINSP2 terminal. It is drawn in the centre-bottom area of the schematic.

MXCS-M9 is a external drawing on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. MXCS-M9 is an external device connection drawing referenced by this schematic for the devices that plug into the 5-pin micro receptacle. Its contents are NOT on this drawing. Function: Documents the external device connections beyond the 5-pin receptacle. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is not applicable - external reference. It is also referred to as MXCS-M9. It is drawn in the off-page area of the schematic.

MXCS-M11 is a external drawing on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. MXCS-M11 is an external device connection drawing referenced by this schematic for the devices that plug into the 5-pin micro receptacle. Its contents are NOT on this drawing. Function: Documents the external device connections beyond the 5-pin receptacle. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is not applicable - external reference. It is also referred to as MXCS-M11. It is drawn in the off-page area of the schematic.

MXCS-P9 is a external drawing on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. MXCS-P9 is an external device connection drawing referenced by this schematic for the devices that plug into the 5-pin micro receptacle. Its contents are NOT on this drawing. Function: Documents the external device connections beyond the 5-pin receptacle. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is not applicable - external reference. It is also referred to as MXCS-P9. It is drawn in the off-page area of the schematic.

MXCS-P11 is a external drawing on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. MXCS-P11 is an external device connection drawing referenced by this schematic for the devices that plug into the 5-pin micro receptacle. Its contents are NOT on this drawing. Function: Documents the external device connections beyond the 5-pin receptacle. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is not applicable - external reference. It is also referred to as MXCS-P11. It is drawn in the off-page area of the schematic.

UPSTREAM-MACHINE is a external machine on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. The upstream (previous / infeed) Mod-Linx machine that plugs into INFEED INTERFACE #1. Not documented on this drawing. This sheet is the MASTER machine, so in a typical installation there may be no previous machine. Function: Supplies the infeed-side start/stop, common, permissive and inspection signals. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is not applicable - external. It is also referred to as previous machine, infeed machine, upstream conveyor. It is drawn in the off-page area of the schematic.

DOWNSTREAM-MACHINE is a external machine on drawing PS20115MLM4-2. The downstream (subordinate / discharge) Mod-Linx machine that plugs into DISCHARGE INTERFACE #1. Not documented on this drawing. Net 130 - the CR-SW coil return - only completes through this machine, which is why CR-SW cannot be energized from anything shown on this sheet alone. Function: Completes the CR-SW coil return (net 130) and receives signal 111. It operates in the control_signal power domain. Its normal state is not applicable - external. It is also referred to as subordinate machine, discharge machine, downstream conveyor, next machine. It is drawn in the off-page area of the schematic.
PLG1:B is a connection point on component PLG1. It serves as a line terminal. It is tied to net L1.
PLG1:W is a connection point on component PLG1. It serves as a neutral terminal. It is tied to net N.
PLG1:G is a connection point on component PLG1. It serves as a ground terminal. It is tied to net GND.
PLG2:B is a connection point on component PLG2. It serves as a line terminal. It is tied to net L1.
PLG2:W is a connection point on component PLG2. It serves as a neutral terminal. It is tied to net N.
PLG2:G is a connection point on component PLG2. It serves as a ground terminal. It is tied to net GND.
TB-L1:1 is a connection point on component TB-L1. It serves as a line terminal. It is tied to net L1.
TB-N:1 is a connection point on component TB-N. It serves as a neutral terminal. It is tied to net N.
TB-GND-A:1 is a connection point on component TB-GND-A. It serves as a ground terminal. It is tied to net GND.
DISC1:L1 is a connection point on component DISC1. It serves as a line terminal. It is tied to net L1.
DISC1:T1 is a connection point on component DISC1. It serves as a output terminal. It is tied to net L1-A.
DISC1:L2 is a connection point on component DISC1. It serves as a line terminal. It is not assigned to a net.
DISC1:T2 is a connection point on component DISC1. It serves as a output terminal. It is not assigned to a net.
DISC1:L3 is a connection point on component DISC1. It serves as a neutral terminal. It is tied to net N.

Power supply PS1 converts the 115VAC input to 24VDC and supplies the 24E-1 distribution bus through circuit breaker CB2. Everything on 24E-1 loses power if PS1 fails.
Both minus terminals of power supply PS1 establish the 0V DC common for the assembly.
Input plug PLG1 brings the 115VAC line supply onto net L1.
The L1 terminal feeds output plug PLG2, passing 115VAC through to the next machine.
The 24E-1 bus supplies the speed controller SPD1.
The 24E-1 bus supplies the circuit 1 indicator light, so LT1 being lit shows the 24VDC control circuit is live.
The 24E-1 bus supplies 24VDC out through pin 5 of the external 5-pin receptacle.
Circuit breaker CB1 (8A) is the over-current protection for the 115VAC feed to power supply PS1. If CB1 trips, PS1 loses its input and the entire 24VDC system goes dead.

Circuit breaker CB2 (20A) is the over-current protection for the whole 24VDC distribution bus. If CB2 trips, everything on net 24E-1 loses power: both start/stop switches, the circuit 1 light, the speed controller, all relay coils and the external receptacle.
The panel disconnect DISC1 isolates the 115VAC supply to the power supply section for servicing. It is an isolation device, not an over-current device.
Start/stop switch PB1 actuates relay CR1: pressing PB1 puts 24VDC on net NET-PB1 (printed on the drawing as PB1), which energizes the CR1 coil at terminal A1.
Start/stop switch PB2 actuates relay CR2: pressing PB2 puts 24VDC on net NET-PB2 (printed on the drawing as PB2), which energizes the CR2 coil at terminal A1.

The BYPASS 5A breaker is used as a manual switch, not as over-current protection. Closing it connects the CR-BP coil return (net 125) to net 120. CR-BP energizes only when the bypass switch is closed AND net 120 is pulled to 0V, which requires both CR1 and CR2 to be energized - that is, both start/stop buttons on.
The REVERSE 5A breaker is used as a manual switch, not as over-current protection. Closing it puts 24VDC from the 24E-1 bus onto the DIR net, which commands the drive cards to run in reverse.

The CR-SW coil return is net 130, which leaves this drawing at the discharge interface. Only the downstream (subordinate) machine can complete that return, so CR-SW cannot be energized by anything shown on this sheet alone.
Energizing the CR1 coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 11-14, connecting 0V through to net 121. This is the first half of the two-relay series start/stop chain.
Energizing the CR2 coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 11-14, connecting net 121 through to net 120. With CR1 also energized, this pulls net 120 down to 0V.

Energizing the CR-ON coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 11-14, putting 24VDC from the 24E-1 bus onto the RUN net. The RUN signal reaches the drive cards through the 5-pin receptacle and the machine runs.
Energizing the CR-BP coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 21-24, putting 24VDC from the 24E-1 bus directly onto the RUN net. This is the bypass path: it runs the machine without CR-ON.

Energizing the CR-BP coil (A1-A2) OPENS its normally-closed contact 11-12, breaking the link between net 111 (the signal from the discharge interface) and net 110. While CR-BP is de-energized this contact is closed and 111 is tied to 110.
Energizing the CR-SW coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 11-14, pulling net 110 down to 0V. That energizes the CR-ON coil and runs the machine.

The CR-ON coil sits between the 24E-1 bus (terminal A1) and net 110 (terminal A2). Pulling net 110 down to 0V - by the CR-SW contact 11-14, by the infeed interface, or through the CR-BP normally-closed contact from net 111 - energizes CR-ON and runs the machine.
The plug ground terminal is bonded to protective earth.
The door/power-supply ground terminal is bonded to protective earth.
The power supply chassis ground terminal is bonded to protective earth through the GND terminal block.

Cable CABLE-LT1 is a wire harness on the schematic. Circuit 1 light cable: black 22AWG (24E-1) and blue 22AWG (0V) are used; brown 22AWG and white 22AWG are NOT CONNECTED and must be removed at the insulation with the exposed end heat-shrunk. It bundles the following wires: W023, W044.

Cable CABLE-RECEPT1 is a wire harness on the schematic. 5-pin micro (M12) cordset at the external device receptacle: brown 18AWG (SPD), white 18AWG (0V), blue 18AWG (24E-1), black 18AWG (RUN), grey 18AWG (DIR). It bundles the following wires: W033, W035, W037, W056.

Cable CABLE-DISCHARGE1 is a wire harness on the schematic. Discharge interface #1 6-pin mini cable: blue 16AWG (111), green 16AWG (0V), red 16AWG (120), orange 16AWG (130), black 16AWG (DINSP1), white 16AWG (DINSP2). It bundles the following wires: W061, W067, W068, W069, W070, W071.

SUB-115VAC-INPUT is a functional section of the assembly. 115VAC single-phase input and isolation section: the supply plugs, the L1/N/GND terminals, the panel disconnect and breaker CB1. It comprises the components: PLG1, PLG2, TB-L1, TB-N, TB-GND-A, DISC1, CB1.

SUB-24VDC-SUPPLY is a functional section of the assembly. 24VDC generation and distribution section: the power supply, its output breaker, the two 24E-1 distribution terminal blocks and the 0V common strip. It comprises the components: PS1, CB2, TB-GND-B, DOOR-GND, EARTH, TB-24E1-A, TB-24E1-B, TB-0V.

SUB-OPERATOR-CONTROL is a functional section of the assembly. Operator start/stop control: both lighted start/stop switches, their spare terminals, the relays they drive and the circuit-1 indicator light. It comprises the components: PB1, PB2, TB-PB1SP, TB-PB2SP, CR1, CR2, LT1, TB-120.

SUB-BYPASS is a functional section of the assembly. Bypass control circuit: the bypass breaker used as a manual switch and the run bypass relay it energizes. It comprises the components: BYPASS-CB, CR-BP.

SUB-RUN-CONTROL is a functional section of the assembly. Run control circuit: the run relay, the switch relay, the run terminal and the 110/130 signal terminal blocks. It comprises the components: CR-ON, CR-SW, TB-RUN, TB-110, TB-130.

SUB-SPEED-DIRECTION is a functional section of the assembly. Speed and direction section: the speed controller, the reverse breaker used as a manual switch, and their signal terminals. It comprises the components: SPD1, TB-SPD, REVERSE-CB, TB-DIR.

SUB-MACHINE-INTERFACE is a functional section of the assembly. External and machine-to-machine interfaces: the 5-pin device receptacle, the infeed and discharge 6-pin interfaces and the inspection-signal terminals. It comprises the components: RECEPT1, INFEED1, DISCHARGE1, TB-IINSP1, TB-IINSP2, TB-DINSP1, TB-DINSP2.

Power supply PS1 converts the 115VAC input to 24VDC and supplies the 24E-1 distribution bus through circuit breaker CB2. Everything on 24E-1 loses power if PS1 fails.
Both minus terminals of power supply PS1 establish the 0V DC common for the assembly.
Input plug PLG1 brings the 115VAC line supply onto net L1.
The L1 terminal feeds output plug PLG2, passing 115VAC through to the next machine.
The 24E-1 bus supplies the speed controller SPD1.
The 24E-1 bus supplies the circuit 1 indicator light, so LT1 being lit shows the 24VDC control circuit is live.
The 24E-1 bus supplies 24VDC out through pin 5 of the external 5-pin receptacle.
Circuit breaker CB1 (8A) is the over-current protection for the 115VAC feed to power supply PS1. If CB1 trips, PS1 loses its input and the entire 24VDC system goes dead.

Circuit breaker CB2 (20A) is the over-current protection for the whole 24VDC distribution bus. If CB2 trips, everything on net 24E-1 loses power: both start/stop switches, the circuit 1 light, the speed controller, all relay coils and the external receptacle.
The panel disconnect DISC1 isolates the 115VAC supply to the power supply section for servicing. It is an isolation device, not an over-current device.
Start/stop switch PB1 actuates relay CR1: pressing PB1 puts 24VDC on net NET-PB1 (printed on the drawing as PB1), which energizes the CR1 coil at terminal A1.
Start/stop switch PB2 actuates relay CR2: pressing PB2 puts 24VDC on net NET-PB2 (printed on the drawing as PB2), which energizes the CR2 coil at terminal A1.

The BYPASS 5A breaker is used as a manual switch, not as over-current protection. Closing it connects the CR-BP coil return (net 125) to net 120. CR-BP energizes only when the bypass switch is closed AND net 120 is pulled to 0V, which requires both CR1 and CR2 to be energized - that is, both start/stop buttons on.
The REVERSE 5A breaker is used as a manual switch, not as over-current protection. Closing it puts 24VDC from the 24E-1 bus onto the DIR net, which commands the drive cards to run in reverse.

The CR-SW coil return is net 130, which leaves this drawing at the discharge interface. Only the downstream (subordinate) machine can complete that return, so CR-SW cannot be energized by anything shown on this sheet alone.
Energizing the CR1 coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 11-14, connecting 0V through to net 121. This is the first half of the two-relay series start/stop chain.
Energizing the CR2 coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 11-14, connecting net 121 through to net 120. With CR1 also energized, this pulls net 120 down to 0V.

Energizing the CR-ON coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 11-14, putting 24VDC from the 24E-1 bus onto the RUN net. The RUN signal reaches the drive cards through the 5-pin receptacle and the machine runs.
Energizing the CR-BP coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 21-24, putting 24VDC from the 24E-1 bus directly onto the RUN net. This is the bypass path: it runs the machine without CR-ON.

Energizing the CR-BP coil (A1-A2) OPENS its normally-closed contact 11-12, breaking the link between net 111 (the signal from the discharge interface) and net 110. While CR-BP is de-energized this contact is closed and 111 is tied to 110.
Energizing the CR-SW coil (A1-A2) closes its normally-open contact 11-14, pulling net 110 down to 0V. That energizes the CR-ON coil and runs the machine.

The CR-ON coil sits between the 24E-1 bus (terminal A1) and net 110 (terminal A2). Pulling net 110 down to 0V - by the CR-SW contact 11-14, by the infeed interface, or through the CR-BP normally-closed contact from net 111 - energizes CR-ON and runs the machine.
